summary: Full-extraction pass over the 20 Nauru documents in batch cbi-nru1 (laws, regulations, Iruwa notices, programme web pages, budget papers and speeches, IMF 2025 Article IV). Adds the remaining fee schedules (pre- and post-approval additions, 2026 filing/approval fees), advertised prices on the 2025 and 2026 price pages and the COP29 release, numeric rules of the 2024 Act and regulations, the IMF's comparison table and visa-free chart (OCR), the FY2025-26 budget and 55% non-tax share, One IMF chart has no printed values and is left as a to-do.

ledger.contains: Nauruan Community Ordinance Amendment Act 1997 (No. 11 of 1997, 6 scanned pages, read by OCR): creates the 'Citizen Investor' category (s. 5(6)-(9)): applicant aged at least 20, of good character and health, investment 'of such form and in such amount as determined by Cabinet' (no amount printed), personal examination by a five-member Nauru Citizen Investment Board (quorum three) that recommends to Cabinet; spouse and minor children eligible; passport on application. Also makes earlier members of the Nauruan Community citizens and covers citizenship for foreign wives of Nauruans (not programme). Clerk's and Speaker's certificates dated 13 June 1997. Creation event already recorded; age and board size added as rules.

Nauru Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Act 2024 (No. 15, certified 20 Aug 2024, 16 pp.): definitions (dependants incl. children 18-30 and parents/grandparents over 55, siblings); eligibility (age 18+, contribution, Cabinet criteria); applications only via licensed agents with application and due-diligence fees; Program and Program Office (may have branches abroad; contribution paid to the Treasury Fund after the agent fee); annual independent audit (auditor appointed within 1 month of year end); annual list of grants to the Registrar by 31 July; agent licensing and penalties ($10,000 or 2 years for individuals, $50,000 for companies); revocation for fees unpaid 30 days; certificate and oath; renunciation (18+); cancellation grounds, 7-day show-cause, 30-day return of certificate, no refunds; register; 7-year record keeping; confidentiality. No amounts of contribution or fees (left to regulations). Certification event already recorded; numeric rules added as terms.

Amendment Act No. 50 of 2025 (certified 23 Dec 2025, 4 pp.): new 'Dependent' definition without age limits; new s. 9 (contribution set by Cabinet; agent fee and Program Office administration fee deducted before payment to the Treasury Fund; Cabinet may designate Special Projects with temporary discounts specifying amount, split and number of applications or duration; due diligence fees cannot be cut); regulations power and electronic applications/records (new ss. 30-31). No amounts. Legal event already recorded; dependant definition added as a rule.

Amendment Act No. 13 of 2026 (certified 31 Mar 2026, 2 pp.): 'Minister' becomes the Minister responsible for the Program Office; Minister may refuse citizenship directly where requirements are not met; consequential change to Regulation 16(5)-(6). No numbers. Event already recorded.

Gazette No. 36 (3 Feb 2026), SL 4 of 2026: Cabinet designates 'The Iruwa Initiative' special project (Cabinet resolution 29 Jan 2026) to mark the programme's first anniversary: main-applicant contribution cut from USD 115,000 to USD 90,000 from 29 Jan to 30 Jun 2026, other fees unchanged, applies to accepted applications not yet paid. Term and event already recorded; nothing else in it.
Gazette No. 197 (5 Jun 2026), SL 28 of 2026: Cabinet Resolution 539/2026 of 3 Jun 2026 extends the Iruwa Initiative to 31 Dec 2026. Term and event already recorded; nothing else in it.

Programme website 'Contribution' page, Wayback capture 25 Jan 2025: contribution (single USD 105,000; family up to four 110,000; five or more 115,000; each sibling 15,000), application fees (25,000 / 27,500 / 30,000), due diligence fees (10,000 principal; 7,500 per dependant 16+), passport fee 500, typical processing 3-4 months; contact details of the Program Office in Nauru and Auckland. All prices and the processing time now recorded.

Programme website 'Contribution' page as of 2 Oct 2026: limited-time offer (USD 25,000 discount from 3 Feb 2026 for applications filed before 31 Dec 2026; principal applicant USD 90,000), USD 2,000 per dependant 16+, 15,000 per sibling; application fees 5,000 + 2,000 per dependant; due diligence 6,000 / 3,000 per dependant 16+ / 3,000 benefactor; bank due diligence fee and transaction charge 1,200 / 1,700 / 2,200 / 1,000 (benefactor); passport 500; typical processing 3-4 months; office addresses. All prices and the processing time now recorded (the 90,000 term was already there).

Program Office press release on the COP29 launch in Baku (13 Nov 2024): quotes from the Climate Minister, the Director of Compliance, the President and Henley & Partners' CEO; processing 3-4 months; visa-free access to 89 destinations; Henley & Partners mandated to design, set up and run the programme (its own claims of 20+ governments advised and USD 15 billion raised are about the firm, not this programme, and are not recorded); notes to editors: minimum age 18, contributions 105,000 / 110,000 / 115,000 / 15,000 per sibling, application fees 25,000 / 27,500 / 30,000, due diligence 10,000 / 7,500 per family member 16+, passport fee 500; interview required. Launch event already recorded; prices, visa-free count and processing time added.

Government Information Office media release (1 Dec 2024) on the President's launch of the programme at the 18th Global Citizenship Conference in Singapore (28 Nov): visa-free access to 89 destinations; contributions to fund coastal protection, renewable energy, agriculture, water and biodiversity; legislation requires FATF-aligned criteria. Other numbers are not about the programme (UN MVI rank 5th, Higher Ground Initiative relocating 90 per cent of families, Intergenerational Trust Fund nearly US$300 million locked until 2033). Launch event already recorded; visa-free count added.

IMF Country Report 25/275 (Nauru 2025 Article IV, 81 pp.). Programme content: press release and staff appraisal calling for vigilance on AML/CFT risks of the citizenship programme and prudent revenue projections (pp. 3, 16, 19-20, 46, 68, 80); authorities say low take-up reflects strict criteria (p. 20); Annex VI (pp. 54-58): programme description (minimum US$105,000, visa-free/on-arrival access to 90 countries, 3-4 months), authorities' expectation of US$5.7 million from over 60 applications in the first year and aspiration of about 20 percent of revenue (over US$43 million), FY2025 actual AU$0.24 million (<0.1% of GDP); Annex Table 1 (inception year, minimum investment and processing time for KNA, DMA, ATG, GRD, LCA, VUT, NRU); Annex Figure 1 (visa-free destinations, 7 countries, OCR); Figure 2 (CBI fiscal revenue % of GDP: first year, peak, latest, 7 countries); cross-country risks (revenue typically 2-4% of GDP over the medium term, a general statement not tied to one programme, not recorded; Vanuatu inflows 14% of GDP in 2020 to about 3% now). The macro-fiscal tables have no citizenship line. Rest of the report: macroeconomy, RPC revenue, banking, fisheries, climate, debt sustainability (not programme). Existing rows kept; added aspiration figures, processing times, visa-free counts, minimum prices and Vanuatu inflows.

ledger.contains: Nauru 2025-26 Budget Paper No. 1 (110 pp.). Programme content: foreword and outlook text (pp. 5, 7-9, 21: 'slow start in 2024-25', revenue to exceed targets, 'visa fees from the Citizenship Investment program'); revenue line 1016 'Citizenship Investment Program' in Table 1.16 (p. 24: 2024-25 approved and revised budget 9,000,000, YTD actual 240,000, 2025-26 budget 9,000,000), Table 1.18 (p. 26: 2023-24 preliminary actual 0, 2024-25 actual 240,000) and Head 16 Finance-Other Payments (p. 62: revised budget 9,000,000, actual + commitment '-', 2025-26 budget 9,000,000, column mislabelled '2026-27 Proposed'). No programme expenditure line. Rest: whole-of-government budget (revenue aggregates, other fees, departmental appropriations, passport fees and a 3,000-passport order for all Nauruan passports) not programme-specific. All programme numbers now recorded (2023-24 zero added; 240,000 and the 9,000,000 budgets were already there).

Naoero 2026-27 Budget Paper No. 1 (95 pp.). Programme content: policy text naming NECRIP (pp. 7, 15, 38, 41: alternative revenue, 'strategic pricing'); p. 9 FY2025-26 performance: 55% of projected non-tax revenue, $3.4 million received against $9 million, shortfall blamed on competition, USD/AUD rate and processing delays; p. 45 text ($9.0 million projection for 2026-27, 'second full year of operations') and Table 1.17 line 1016 (2024-25 '-', 2025-26 approved and revised 9,000,000, YTD actual 3,740,599, 2026-27 budget 9,000,000), repeated in Table 1.19 (p. 47) and Head 16 (p. 67). Scenario chart (p. 15) has no programme values. Rest: whole-of-government budget, not programme. Added the FY2025-26 budget and the 55% share; YTD actual, $3.4 million and the 2026-27 budget were already recorded.

Nauru 2025-26 Budget Paper No. 2 (39 pp., economic and sector performance): outlook paragraph naming the Citizenship by Investment Programme among new revenues (p. 4) and DCCNR section (p. 39) on the ECRCP launch at COP29, funds earmarked for climate adaptation, programme designed and run with Henley & Partners. No programme numbers; the rest covers other sectors. Context already in the 29 Aug 2025 budget event.

President's 2025-26 Appropriation Bill second reading speech (29 Aug 2025, 20 pp.): p. 6 on the programme (drawing interest, first successful applicants being issued passports, Henley & Partners expect more applicants, revenue to exceed expectations after a slow 2024-25, awareness of reputational risk). No programme numbers; other figures are about the budget, trust fund, Australia treaty, health and education. Event already recorded.

President's 2026-27 Appropriation Bill second reading speech (20 Jul 2026, 17 pp.): p. 7 non-tax revenue $19.4 million incl. $9 million projected from the programme; first full year FY2025-26: 103 applications (about 9 a month), $3.7 million received against a $9 million budget, 52 approved, 9 rejected, rest in process or withdrawn; discounted pricing introduced; programme expected to rival fisheries revenue within three to five years (not a number to record). Rest: budget aggregates, RPC, social measures, CRVAA etc. Added the 2026-27 projection; the other counts were already recorded. The 'approximately 9 applications per month' average is not recorded as a row, because it would sit beside the 103 for the same indicator and year and read as a conflicting figure.

Explanatory memorandum to the Amendment Bill 2026 (1 p.): explains clauses 1-6 (Minister definition per Administrative Arrangements Order 2026; Minister may refuse grants; consequential change to Regulation 16). No numbers; the change is recorded as the 31 Mar 2026 event from the Act.

Second reading speech by Minister Maverick Eoe (31 Mar 2026, 2 pp.): describes the previous rejection route (Program Office -> Registrar -> Minister -> Cabinet) and the Bill letting the Minister refuse directly to cut delays. No numbers; recorded as the 31 Mar 2026 event from the Act.

Amendment Regulations No. 2 of 2026 (Gazette No. 32, certified 29 Jan 2026, 25 pp.): new definitions; agent forms; reg. 9A filing fees on submission, approval fees on approval in principle; police certificates (16+, six months' residence in past 10 years); new reg. 16 (Registrar endorsement, Minister, Cabinet); reg. 17 (approval fees within 30 days; agent fee and administration fee deducted from contribution); Part 4A electronic forms, lodgement (after 11:59 pm counts as next business day), signatures, notices, records; reg. 33 additional fees set by the Program Office; reg. 34 special projects; new Schedule 1 (application 5,000 + 2,000 per dependant; due diligence 6,000 / 3,000 / 3,000 benefactor; contribution 115,000 + 2,000 per dependant 16+ + 15,000 per sibling; passport 500); Schedule 2 (pre-approval additions); Schedule 3 (post-approval additions: application 5,000 each, due diligence 6,000, contributions 30,000 spouse, 0 child up to 2 and recently adopted child, 25,000 child 3-18 and grandchild, 35,000 others, passport 500); Schedule 4 (agent licence 5,000, agent fee 25,000); Schedule 4A (administration 10,000 / 5,000); Schedules 5-8 replaced by lists of required form contents (agent forms, application forms incl. 10-year address and employment history, oath, certificate, register). All schedule amounts and numeric rules now recorded (six were already there).

Amendment Regulations SL 2 of 2025 (Gazette No. 51, 10 Feb 2025, 35 pp.): agent licence rules (requirements, fee, 1-year licence from issue, renewal applied for 1 month ahead, no new applications after expiry); police certificates (16+, six months' residence within 10 years); false statements; interviews 16+; custody and consent for minors; reg. 16 (grant after contribution remitted); certificate delivery chain; benefactor due diligence fee USD 7,500 in Schedules 1 and 3 (one existing row covers both); substituted agent forms and code of conduct (30-day notice of sub-agents, 25% shareholder/beneficial-owner disclosure), application forms (Form 1 restates contribution and fee bands; Form 2 five-year name-change bar; 10-year address and employment history; medical form) and citizenship affirmation. All amounts and numeric rules now recorded (the Schedule 1 benefactor fee was already there).
